subtopic: Using AI tools for learning without cheating
subtype: Approach: correcting course after crossing the line [Revision]
passage: I'm Aditi, and I'll be honest: I submitted a history assignment that was about ninety percent AI. I told myself I'd rewrite it later. I didn't. Three days later the class was discussing my topic and I couldn't say a word, and I felt sick, not because I might get caught, but because it wasn't mine. That evening I decided to tell Yusuf Sir before anyone asked. I walked to the staffroom with cold hands and said it straight. He was quiet, then said, “Thank you for telling me, beti.” I would lose the marks for that submission and had to redo it. I said, “I know.” I rewrote it that week in my own words, slowly and badly at first. And I made a rule: AI can explain, never write. The mark was lower. But I can talk about that topic now.

qa.q: What did Aditi decide to do that evening?
qa.a: Aditi decided to tell Yusuf Sir before anyone asked.

qa.q: What was Aditi feeling when she could not say a word in class?
qa.a: Aditi felt sick with guilt, since the work was not hers.

qa.q: Which choice worked in Aditi's story, and why?
qa.a: Telling the teacher and redoing the work in her own words worked, because it fixed the problem and the learning finally happened.

qa.q: How might Yusuf Sir see Aditi's confession?
qa.a: Yusuf Sir probably appreciates her honesty, since he thanks her, even as he applies the consequence.

grounding: A teen who submitted mostly AI-written work realises it was wrong, tells the teacher, redoes it in her own words and sets a rule, accepting a consequence.
